post.description: This event is triggered when a user is created.

id.description: The unique identifier of the user

primary_email_verified.description: Whether the primary email has been verified to belong to this user

primary_email_auth_enabled.description: Whether the primary email is used for authentication. If this is set to `false`, the user will not be able to sign in with the primary email with password or OTP

display_name.description: Human-readable user display name. This is not a unique identifier.

created_at_millis.description: The time the team was created (the number of milliseconds since epoch, January 1, 1970, UTC)

server_metadata.description: Server metadata. Used as a data store, only accessible from the server side. You can store secret information related to the team here.

id.description: The unique identifier of the team

display_name.description: Human-readable team display name. This is not a unique identifier.

profile_image_url.description: URL of the profile image for team. Can be a Base64 encoded image. Must be smaller than 100KB. Please compress and crop to a square before passing in.

client_metadata.description: Client metadata. Used as a data store, accessible from the client side. Do not store information that should not be exposed to the client.

client_read_only_metadata.description: Client read-only, server-writable metadata. Used as a data store, accessible from the client side. Do not store information that should not be exposed to the client. The client can read this data, but cannot modify it. This is useful for things like subscription status.

selected_team_id.description: ID of the team currently selected by the user

profile_image_url.description: URL of the profile image for user. Can be a Base64 encoded image. Must be smaller than 100KB. Please compress and crop to a square before passing in.

signed_up_at_millis.description: The time the user signed up (identify) => `(the number of milliseconds since epoch, January 1, 1970, UTC)`

client_metadata.description: Client metadata. Used as a data store, accessible from the client side. Do not store information that should not be exposed to the client.

client_read_only_metadata.description: Client read-only, server-writable metadata. Used as a data store, accessible from the client side. Do not store information that should not be exposed to the client. The client can read this data, but cannot modify it. This is useful for things like subscription status.

server_metadata.description: Server metadata. Used as a data store, only accessible from the server side. You can store secret information related to the user here.

last_active_at_millis.description: The time the user was last active (identify) => `(the number of milliseconds since epoch, January 1, 1970, UTC)`

is_restricted.description: Whether the user is in restricted state (has signed up but not completed onboarding requirements)

restricted_reason.description: The reason why the user is restricted (e.g., type: "email_not_verified", "anonymous", or "restricted_by_administrator"), null if not restricted

restricted_by_admin.description: Whether the user is restricted by an administrator. Can be set manually or by sign-up rules.

restricted_by_admin_reason.description: Public reason shown to the user explaining why they are restricted. Optional.

restricted_by_admin_private_details.description: Private details about the restriction (e.g., which sign-up rule triggered). Only visible to server access and above.

country_code.description: Best-effort ISO country code captured at sign-up time from request geo headers.

risk_scores.description: User risk scores used for sign-up risk evaluation.

post.description: This event is triggered the first time an error is grouped into a new issue. It does not fire again for subsequent occurrences of the same issue.

id.description: The unique identifier of the issue

short_id.description: Per-project monotonic counter identifying the issue, as a decimal string (it is a 64-bit integer and does not fit a JSON number safely)

type.description: The error type, eg. the constructor name of the thrown error

culprit.description: The code location the issue was attributed to

level.description: The severity the occurrence was reported with

status.description: The lifecycle status of the issue

substatus.description: A finer-grained view of an unresolved issue, derived from its timestamps

first_seen_at_millis.description: When the issue was first seen, in milliseconds since epoch

last_seen_at_millis.description: When the issue was most recently seen, in milliseconds since epoch

times_seen.description: Lifetime occurrence count, as a decimal string (it is a 64-bit integer and does not fit a JSON number safely)

service_name.description: The service that reported the issue, if configured

environment.description: The environment the issue was reported from, if configured

release.description: The release the issue was reported from, if configured

url.description: Deep link to the issue in the Hexclave dashboard
